metadata.title: Why it 'doesn't pay' to be bullish on Apple's stock ahead of the event, according to an analyst - MarketWatch

content.text:
49 min ago
Why it 'doesn't pay' to be bullish on Apple's stock ahead of the event, according to an analyst
Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event may not offer much glimmer to the stock, at least based on past performance.
Over the past five years, Apple's average stock performance on the day a new iPhone is announced is -0.72% , according to Keybanc analyst Brandon Nispel. He added that losses extend to a 1.22% decline over the five days following an iPhone event. Going back to 2007, just six of Apple's iPhone events have led to a stock bump, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
"We believe given Apple is one of the world's most well-reported-on companies, announcements at the event rarely are surprising to investors and it doesn't pay to be bullish going into the event," Nispel said in a recent note to clients. Keybanc has the equivalent of a sell rating on Apple's stock.
